Audit 2026-11-03: Native consent and no prompt loop: the screenshot portal owns first-request consent and an explicit NotAllowed/AccessDenied returns capture-permission-denied once (PortalScreenshotTest::executionPreservesPrePipelineOutcomes denied row, PortalScreenshotTest::denialOffersPermissionGuidanceOnceAndNeverRepromptsOrLeavesOutput asserts one portal call, one capturePermissionDenied signal after settling, no overlay and no output). The denial now offers a 'How to allow screen capture' dialog (app/CapturePermissionHelp.cpp, wired in CaptureFeature) explaining GNOME Settings > Privacy, KDE System Settings > Privacy and 'flatpak permission-reset com.xerahs.app' for the portal store, with an Open Settings action that starts gnome-control-center privacy or systemsettings detached when found on PATH (the desktop's own app is preferred). CapturePermissionHelpTest covers both branches with injected PATH and launcher: route selection by desktop and availability, launching with the right program/arguments while the guidance stays open, a visible launch failure, manual-only guidance with no Open Settings action when no settings app exists, and a single dialog however many denials arrive. Linux has no universal settings UI for the portal permission store, so the manual steps are the documented route there.
